Literature can be broadly categorized into two main branches based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods and two-stage pipelines. In the latter category, CNN regresses intermediate cues such as object coordinates or virtual control points instead of pose parameters in the initial stage. Object pose is then resolved through the construction of correspondence constraints in the subsequent stage. This study proposes a one-stage CNN framework utilizing intermediate cues based on absolute coordinates of three real control points. These control points are defined on the object's surface and are distinct from those used in projection-based correspondence construction. The network directly predicts the absolute coordinates of the real control points and corresponding projection points in the image. Subsequent object pose estimation is then obtained through the unique solution of a projective constraint system derived from the real and projected points. Comprehensive experiments conducted on three datasets demonstrate that our proposed one-stage framework surpasses the performance of two-stage baseline methods. Moreover, the results demonstrate that our method is on par with cutting-edge two-stage approaches and outperforms state-of-the-art one-stage methods with minimal computational expense. To compensate for these difficulties, doctors often rely on supplementary information from other imaging techniques such as endoscopy. This suggests that there may be value in using readily available visual information from these procedures as a means of improving tumor detection from CT scans with the aid of interactive tools. To explore this idea, we have developed an efficient system for automatically segmenting the esophagus from CT scans in the presence of tumors, based on a combination of low-cost visual data from endoscopy, interactively selected regions, and the esophagus's inherent shape. To train and evaluate our system, we have collected a relatively small dataset consisting of six CT scans and matching endoscopy images, along with manually drawn boundaries of the esophagus. This dataset is used to test two different variants of our system, which involves a series of straightforward interactive and semi-supervised processes to refine the accuracy of the esophagus's shape and tumor detection. Our experiments demonstrate that this approach results in significantly better performance compared to several established medical image processing algorithms, as well as the use of visual information from endoscopy alone. Furthermore, this system provides a practical solution for clinicians to easily extend its capabilities to a larger patient population with minimal additional training required. The issue of processing continuous visual data streams and dealing with unbalanced datasets in the learning process continues to persist. Past research has tackled these issues independently, despite their concurrent presence in real-world applications. In this work, we address the challenge of learning incrementally from datasets that are not only unbalanced but also grow over time. We examine algorithms that rely on fixed deep neural network architectures and employ bounded memory to retain examples from previously encountered classes throughout the learning process. Given that the memory is finite, older classes are forgotten as new classes are encountered, mirroring the incremental learning process observed in real-world environments. A key characteristic of these learning processes is the formation of distinct memory clusters, where each cluster corresponds to a class and encompasses a subset of the retained examples. We evaluate several existing deep neural network architectures and propose an innovative method that adapts batch normalization to operate over memory clusters rather than mini-batches. we studied a distant starburst galaxy, examining how star formation-driven gas outflows are linked to other properties of the galaxy. Our data show a nearly linear relationship between outflow mass and star formation rates, as well as a significant correlation between outflow mass and gas usage times. In regions of high gas usage within the galaxy, the outflow mass increases substantially, characteristic of its ability to resist collapse and form new stars. etime, research has focused on conformal matter collineations within the energy-momentum tensor. The overall structure of these collineations is determined under non-degenerate conditions, with fifteen distinct, independent forms found. However, when the energy-momentum tensor becomes degenerate, the associated conformal collineations exhibit infinite degrees of freedom. Moreover, specific degenerate subcases may still harbor non-degenerate Ricci inheritance collineations. A degenerate energy-momentum tensor is characteristic of spacetimes experiencing cosmic censorship, where the Ricci inheritance collineations play a crucial role in revealing and classifying potential singularities hidden by horizons. A new, broader framework for studying black hole singularities is thus established. Within this framework, fifteen parameters associated with the Ricci inheritance collineations on the Einstein tensor serve as the matter field inputs. A key advantage of this approach is its ability to bypass the complicated process of solving the Einstein field equations. Instead, researchers can directly determine the Ricci inheritance collineations on the Einstein tensor at specific spacetime locations, effectively providing a bridge between the mathematical properties of conformal collineations and the physical features of black hole singularities. A detailed analysis is conducted for Schwarzschild, Reissner-Nordstr\"om, and Van Stockum spacetimes to illustrate this framework's applicability. The previously overlooked degenerate case of the Einstein tensor, resulting from the Van Stockum metric, is also explicitly determined for the first time.

graphene holds significant promise, enabling the synthesis of highly lattice-mismatched materials and reducing waste from expensive substrate reuse. Nevertheless, concrete proof of a remote epitaxial process is yet to be found. Many instances are instead attributed to contaminants between graphene and the substrate, or alternative processes such as van der Waals epitaxy. This study discovered that when growing the Heusler compound GdPtSb on clean graphene substrates, it results in a unique 30 degree rotated superstructure, not explicable through other mechanisms. This rotation domain percentage significantly increases at lower growth temperatures. It's suggested that slower surface diffusion at lower temperatures favors the remote epitaxial process over faster surface diffusion at higher temperatures. Moreover, this study demonstrated that precise annealing of the graphene and consideration of film/substrate lattice mismatches are crucial for achieving epitaxial relationships with a range of Heusler compounds, including LaPtSb and GdAuGe. The distinctive 30 degree rotated superstructure offers a potential experimental signature for identifying remote epitaxy. This discovery paves the way for exploring this process and the associated advantages in van der Waals epitaxy systems.

Deep neural network-based classifiers have a common issue, however - they often provide predictions that seem excessively certain but do not reflect the true likelihood of classification accuracy. This limitation is attributed to the inherent closed-world nature of traditional softmax formulation. As cross-entropy loss encourages models to classify inputs into pre-defined categories, rather than modeling the true posterior probabilities, this has resulted in an ongoing concern. This new model, known as the Generalized Mean Editor (GME), has been shown to enhance the confidence calibration of existing models while providing an interesting comparison to the stacking method. Current methods of weather prediction, using either a network of sensors or a vehicle-mounted camera, are limited in scope and costly.
A robust weather detection system is crucial for seamless operation of transportation services in diverse weather conditions.
However, this task is complex due to the varied nature of weather and the scarcity of distinct features in visual data.
Existing approaches to weather detection are largely confined to specific weather types and the available datasets are limited, making the development of a universal weather detection system challenging.
In this paper, a novel method for weather classification is presented, using a unique algorithm called progressive largest receptive field (PLRF) in combination with a comprehensive dataset containing multiple weather types.
The proposed approach involves a progressive process of weather classification, starting from a general decision about the primary weather characteristic (such as rain, snow, or sun) and then refining the classification based on secondary features.

Menger developed an interest in the abstract concept of angle function, which he then generalized for use in metric and semi-metric spaces. Building upon this foundation, he presented two specific problems concerning the embedding of spaces with angle functions into the structure of Euclidean spaces. Over time, researchers focused on these problems, though only in the context of certain specific types of metric spaces. This article aims to enhance the definition of angle function to accommodate spaces with the property of betweenness, which it deems a more fundamental framework. Within this revised framework, the article provides solutions to Menger's initially presented problems. Furthermore, the article offers a solution to the previously unaddressed first problem of Menger, which had been stated in the context of spaces with the property of betweenness. This solution, the article presents, is a more comprehensive answer to the initially posed question. The article also provides a solution to the second problem of Menger, which had been stated in the context of spaces with angle functions, and which had been previously answered by researchers with a solution different from the one proposed in the article for the first problem. The article also presents another solution to the second problem of Menger. The article also presents a solution to a problem of H. Stocker, which had been stated in the context of spaces with angle functions. The article provides definitions of certain terms which had been used in the solutions to the problems, using a definition that is more fundamental than the definition used in the original paper

Focusing on the varying effects of remote learning on diverse demographic groups, data was collected from online learning modules in the Fall 2020 and Spring 2020 semesters. Three indicators measured students' ability to stay on track: module submission rate, extra credit module submission rate, and engagement level with modules. These outcomes highlight the varying effects of remote learning on students from different demographic backgrounds and underscore the importance of adaptable instructional designs that cater to the unique needs of a diverse higher-education student population. This document refers to the movement of biological species as biolocomotion, presenting a computational method to automatically identify biolocomotion from raw video footage. Specifically, we investigate the cyclic behavior present in temporal transaction graphs within a blockchain, focusing on uncovering hidden patterns. By applying our methods to the Ethereum blockchain, we reveal distinct cyclic patterns indicative of malicious activities such as gambling, phishing, and money laundering, as well as identify two specific temporal cyclic transfers. Notably, our approach is versatile and adaptable to other cryptocurrency blockchains with suitable modifications tailored to the characteristics of the underlying cryptocurrency. Moreover, our results demonstrate the efficacy of our method in detecting the mentioned malicious activities with high precision, revealing that the approach can identify these patterns across various blockchain datasets with minimal error rate below 5%. We make available the source code for our money trail analysis module, as well as the processed and raw data used in the gambling and phishing sections of the paper at the following URL: https://github.com/aliemam/money-trail-analysis. Additionally, we present a interactive visualizer for the temporal transaction graphs and the money trails at the following URL: https://emam-ali.com

In this research, we focus on estimating non-negative discrete variables using rounded averages, specifically when U equals the average of Y divided by n. netting has far-reaching effects on a nation's economy, affecting transactions and business-to-business interactions. Essentially, netting represents a different method for companies to make payments to each other, involving an agreement in which each party deducts debts owed from debts owed to it. By combining the outcomes of all intercompany transactions, netting facilitates streamlined, aggregated payments. In this research, we develop a social network analysis tool to visualize and assess the impact of netting on a nation's economy. By representing each company as a node in the economy's transaction graph and modifying the node values according to the netting agreements, we create a compact, simplified graph that showcases the economy's transactions. Furthermore, our proposed system allows for the detection of potentially vulnerable companies by identifying those with isolated subgraphs resulting from netting. We have successfully applied our methodology to analyze the impact of netting in three major economies: those of the United States, Germany, and Japan. Our results reveal that netting has a significant effect on the economy's transaction graph, significantly reducing the number of nodes and edges. Among the companies covered in our analysis, a substantial proportion are at risk of being isolated as a result of netting. We believe that our methodology and findings can contribute to a deeper understanding of the economy's transaction graphs and the impact of netting on these graphs. By providing a visual representation of the economy's transaction graphs, we can identify patterns and relationships that may not be apparent from financial statements alone. Our results

Ultimately, this concise model is capable of conveying the essence of the statistical mechanics behind the phenomenon of negative absolute temperature, making it an excellent teaching tool for this subject. This report serves as an invitation for the academic community to engage in a broader discussion on the topic, with the goal of exploring further the most effective methods for explaining the concept of negative absolute temperature to students. It is our hope that this discussion may yield the most suitable, practical strategies for teaching this subject in the classroom. Additionally, we present a set of questions that may be presented as assignments to the students, along with a suggested outline for a possible lecture on this topic. This report is accompanied by a document containing the energy level configurations that were graphically represented in the figures, along with the corresponding Boltzmann distributions

In this research, a concept for GAN-based medical imaging enhancement is demonstrated. Though GAN-based techniques excel at natural image creation and manipulation, their potential in medicine remains largely unexplored. Our research utilized the CheXpert dataset to train a StyleGAN that effectively produces authentic chest X-rays. By incorporating an encoder from the AttrGAN algorithm, we successfully marked a patient's condition on a healthy X-ray. By examining real X-rays with the marked condition from the trained generator network, we developed a simple method to train a classifier that accurately identified the marked condition over 90% of the time. This breakthrough suggests that GAN-based medical imaging enhancement may soon become a reality, with implications for reducing data privacy concerns. In particular, researchers can develop and validate models on private patient data without compromising confidentiality. Building upon this work, numerous new applications in disease-aware image editing can be explored. In one such extension, we investigated using GAN-generated data to augment limited datasets for the detection of rare conditions. Although preliminary results show promise, further investigation is needed to confirm findings due to concerns about dataset size and class imbalance. This study's code and findings have been made available for other researchers to build upon and explore new avenues in disease-aware image editing. For domains with irregular boundaries, using a grid without a set pattern to calculate the potential by splitting it into small areas becomes impractical due to high computational costs. In this paper, we propose an efficient and straightforward high-order method for calculating Newtonian potentials based on the Hahn-Banach theorem and duality. By transforming the potential into a surface and boundary integral and applying the Hahn-Banach theorem, we can switch from a complicated volume integral to a more manageable surface integral. Then, using duality, we can switch from an unstable finite element method to a stable boundary collocation method. By transforming the boundary integral into a matrix, we can finally solve for the potential by inverting the matrix. This results in a computationally efficient and straightforward method with a linear computational cost for smooth domains. In addition, we provide an efficient algorithm for constructing the matrix from a set of basis functions. This reduces the memory needed to store the matrix, making it even more computationally efficient. In the end, we demonstrate the accuracy of our method by comparing it to an exact solution. This allows us to also consider an alternative method for constructing the matrix which gives us another option for calculating the matrix. This alternative method produces the same accurate results when compared to the exact solution.
